deities: Sri Venkateswara Swamy (Srinivasa/Balaji/Govinda, presiding deity, standing east-facing)
Sri Devi and Bhu Devi (consorts, represented on the Lord's chest)
festivals: Srivari Brahmotsavam (9-day annual festival, September-October; attracts lakhs of devotees)
Vaikuntha Ekadashi (December-January; darshan through the Vaikunta Dwaram)
Jyesthabhishekam (June, abhishekam of the processional idols)

history.dynasty: Origins attributed to the Tondaiman (Pallava-era) king; expanded under the Cholas (10th century), Pandyas, and the Vijayanagara Empire (notably Krishnadevaraya); managed by Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams since 1933
history.period: Earliest records c. 300 BCE (weak); first recorded endowment 966 CE (Pallava queen Samavai); major Vijayanagara-phase expansion 14th-16th century
history.summary: The Venkateswara Temple at Tirumala, dedicated to Lord Venkateswara (Srinivasa/Balaji), an incarnation of Vishnu believed to reside here through the Kali Yuga, is one of the eight Vishnu Swayambhu kshetras and the 75th Divya Desam. The temple is traditionally attributed to a Tondaiman king and built in Dravidian style from around 300 CE; the first recorded endowment is Pallava queen Samavai's donation in 966 CE, the Cholas expanded the complex, and it gained most of its wealth under the Vijayanagara Empire - Krishnadevaraya gifted gold and jewels in 1517 enabling the gilding of the Ananda Nilayam roof. Saint Ramanujacharya visited Tirupati thrice and streamlined the rituals per the Vaikhanasa Agama tradition. After British-era management through the East India Company and then the Mahants of the Hathiramji Mutt (1843-1933), the Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams was formed under the TTD Act of 1933 and continues to administer the temple. The temple bears 640 inscriptions and a unique collection of ~3,000 copper plates of Annamacharya's sankirtanas; it is among the world's most-visited religious sites (60,000+ devotees daily) and one of the richest Hindu temples.

name: Sri Venkateswara Temple
town_description: Tirumala is a hill town atop the Seshachalam range at about 853 metres, forming the seventh of the seven sacred hills (Venkatadri) and lying about 22 km uphill from the city of Tirupati, the main pilgrimage gateway. Tirupati is a major city in southern Andhra Pradesh with its own airport, railway junction and bus stations, and it hosts important associated shrines (Govindaraja Swamy in the city, Padmavathi Ammavari at Tiruchanur). Tirumala town itself is strictly vegetarian and built entirely around serving the millions of pilgrims visiting the temple.

travel.airport: Tirupati Airport (Renigunta) (approx. 40 km from Tirumala; taxis and cabs available).
travel.railway: Tirupati Junction (approx. 22 km downhill from Tirumala), well connected across India.
travel.road: Tirumala is approx. 22 km uphill from Tirupati city via the ghat road; APSRTC buses run every few minutes, and taxis are widely available. Devotees also walk up on two footpaths: Alipiri Mettu (3,550 steps, approx. 9-11 km, 3-5 hours) and the steeper Srivari Mettu (2,388 steps, approx. 2.1 km, 1.5-2 hours); foot pilgrims receive free Divya Darshan tokens.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for the pleasantest weather. Brahmotsavam (September-October) and Vaikuntha Ekadashi are the most spectacular but draw crowds crossing one lakh; weekdays and early-morning/late-night slots are least crowded.
visitor_information.opening_hours: The temple opens daily around 2:30 AM with Suprabhatam and stays open nearly round the clock until Ekanta Seva around 1:30 AM (verify - the day's schedule shifts with festivals and weekly sevas). Free Sarva Darshan runs through most of the day with brief closures for sevas; Special Entry Darshan costs Rs. 300 (booked online in timed slots); VIP/break darshan and Divya Darshan (for foot pilgrims) operate separately. Strict traditional dress code; mobiles, cameras and footwear not allowed inside.
